messages:
maria: heads-up — the android sample app is hitting a weird auth/ retry interaction on API 31. we see 401, then the client fires the same request twice and the server rejects the second one (idempotency).
anil: can you paste the logs? is this on okhttp 4.x + retrofit 2.9?
maria: yep okhttp 4.9.3 + retrofit 2.9. repro steps: login, then trigger upload via SampleUploader.uploadFile(). intermittent after token expiry. logcat:
	I/HttpClient: --> POST /upload  (auth: Bearer expired_token)
	I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized
	I/AuthInterceptor: refreshing token synchronously
	I/HttpClient: --> POST /upload  (auth: Bearer new_token)
	W/Server: duplicate payload id 0xabc123 - rejected

kevin: is the refresh running inside an Interceptor or an Authenticator?
maria: we implemented token refresh as an interceptor that blocks and calls authService.refresh(). it synchronizes on a TokenProvider.lock to avoid parallel refreshes.
sam: interceptors run on the call stack — if you do a synchronous network call inside an interceptor with the same OkHttp client it can re-enter the dispatcher and cause weird behavior. Authenticator is the intended hook for 401 handling.
jenny: can you share the client config? maybe callTimeout or dispatcher limits are relevant.
maria: client config snippet:

	OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
	  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
	  .readTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
	  .callTimeout(60, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
	  .dispatcher(new Dispatcher(Executors.newFixedThreadPool(20)))
	  .addInterceptor(new AuthInterceptor(tokenProvider))
	  .build();

maria: Retrofit uses client for the refresh call too (we call authService.refresh() implemented by the same Retrofit instance).
anil: that's the issue. doing synchronous refresh with the same client in an interceptor means the refresh call shares the connection pool/dispatcher and can deadlock or duplicate because the original call isn't fully completed until interceptor returns.
kevin: solution I used before: move refresh to a separate OkHttpClient instance with its own dispatcher / connection pool, or use okhttp.Authenticator which gets called when the client receives 401 and is allowed to create a replacement request.
sam: also consider making the token provider return a future and queue awaiting calls instead of reissuing the same original request while the token is updated. you can mark requests that are in-flight and only retry once per call.
jenny: add a note about Android: on API < 29 we sometimes saw connection reuse behave differently; separate client avoids weird keep-alive behaviors across platform versions.
maria: thanks. quick patch i tried locally: swapped interceptor refresh to a dedicated client:

	OkHttpClient authClient = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
	  .connectTimeout(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
	  .dispatcher(new Dispatcher(Executors.newFixedThreadPool(2)))
	  .build();

	// use authRetrofit created with authClient for refresh call

maria: that fixed the duplicate request in my local runs. still hitting one failing case in CI though (race where two calls simultaneously see expired token and both proceed).
kevin: for that race you need to coordinate at the TokenProvider level: use an atomic state machine or a CompletableDeferred in Kotlin to let the first refresher notify waiters.
sam: can we add a small sample to devex/samples/android showcasing the correct pattern? customers keep hitting this and it causes data duplication for uploads.
ji-bot: created issue #2789 in devex with title "android: avoid duplicate requests during token refresh - sample + docs" by maria
ci-bot: CI flake: reproducer tests on Android 11 emulator passed 8/10; failing runs show Dispatcher.queue waiting threads.
maria: i'll send a PR with the dedicated auth client + token-provider coordination and add a test (instrumentation or robolectric).
anil: please include a short note in the README about "don't call your main retrofit client to refresh tokens from an interceptor" and link to okhttp Authenticator example.
maria: will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
